questions.q: Where do the actual selectable values for a Choice-type field live?
options: Directly on the dictionary entry itself, as a comma-separated list
Hard-coded in the platform's source code, not in any table
In a separate table, sys_choice, where each row ties back to a specific table and field
In the sys_db_object table, alongside the table's own definition
questions.explain: The dictionary entry just marks the field's type as Choice; sys_choice holds the individual label/value rows.

questions.q: What does a single sys_choice row carry, at minimum?
options: Only a label, with no separate underlying value
A full copy of every record that currently uses that choice value
The sys_id of every user who has ever selected that option
The table and field it belongs to, a label, a value, and a sequence controlling dropdown order
questions.explain: Table, field, label, value, and sequence are the core attributes of a sys_choice row; it can also be marked inactive.

questions.q: How does Incident's Category/Subcategory dependent-choice behavior actually work under the hood?
options: Each Subcategory sys_choice row carries a parent value, and the form only shows rows whose parent matches the selected Category
Subcategory is a free-text field with no connection to Category at all
Category and Subcategory are actually the same field rendered twice
Dependent choices are hard-coded into the form's HTML and can't be reconfigured
questions.explain: The dependent field's dictionary entry points to the controlling field via Dependent on field, and sys_choice rows carry the parent-value link.

questions.q: What are the five real out-of-box values on Incident's priority Choice field?
options: Open, In Progress, On Hold, Resolved, Closed
1 - Critical, 2 - High, 3 - Moderate, 4 - Low, 5 - Planning
Low, Medium, High, Critical, Planning
P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 with no labels
questions.explain: These are the real out-of-box Incident priority values, each paired with a leading severity number.

questions.q: Why is priority often a misleading example of "a Choice field the agent just picks from a dropdown"?
options: Because priority isn't actually a Choice field at all
Because priority has no sys_choice rows backing it
Because priority is usually calculated from Impact x Urgency through a priority lookup matrix, not chosen directly
Because only administrators are allowed to see the priority field
questions.explain: In a correctly configured instance, Priority is derived from Impact and Urgency via the priority lookup matrix, not hand-picked by the agent.
